newsitem.title: UK: Battered palm oil sinks lower on Euro veg oils.
newsitem.headline: Battered palm oil sinks lower on Euro veg oils.

text.p: Palm oil continued to take a battering on the European vegetable oil market on Thursday as the previous day's sell-off continued.
"Fundamentally palm oil is looking very sick with increasing production and stocks, but no major export business," said one trader.
The new Indonesia export tax structure was also seen as beginning to take its toll on the market.

"The new export tax was seen as bearish, but only in the long term, because high demand in Indonesia was expected to slow the impact, but it now seems people are taking more notice of it," said another trader.
On Monday Indonesia announced a revision of its palm oil export tax structure.
Indonesia originally introduced the tax in September 1994 to ensure sufficient supply and stable prices in the domestic market.
The taxes, announced at the beginning of each month, had been based on a composite average of international prices in the last two weeks of the previous month.
The export taxes will now be calculated on an 'ad valorem' basis, or in proportion to the estimated value of the goods concerned.
During the 1994-1996 period, the export tax on crude palm oil and products ranged between 10 to 12 percent of their export value.
Under the new structure, crude palm oil would be subject to a tax of five percent, RBD palm oil four percent, RBD palm olein two percent and crude olein four percent.
Buying by one major refiner was again seen towards the close of the Malaysian market but it failed to stop the decline.
"People don't know quite what the refiner is up to, whether he is trying to support the market or cover business," said one trader.
At midday crude palm oil cif Europe was $5 to $2.50 lower after Sep traded at $505 a tonne cif.
Products were also $5 to $2.50 down after olein traded at $527.50 for Jul, $525 and $523 for Aug, $525 for Aug/Sep and $522.25 and $522 a tonne fob Malaysian ports for Oct/Dec.
The remainder of the European market was featureless with soy oil sellers mixed at 0.25 guilders up to 0.50 guilders down and rape oil 0.25 guilders up to unchanged.
Coconut oil offers were $5 higher while palmkernel oil was $2.50 up in quiet markets. --Jim Ballantyne, London Newsroom, +44 171 542 8062
